title: Tables and Table Structure
summary: Use table, caption, thead, tbody, tr, th, and td for tabular data.

sketchBlocks.title: Use a table for row-and-column relationships
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Tables are for data where values relate across rows and columns. Use `<table>` for the structure, `<tr>` for each row, `<th>` for header cells, and `<td>` for data cells.

A list is better for a simple collection; a table is better when each row shares the same fields.

tryItExercises.title: Turn the meeting data into table rows
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The meeting information is written as paragraphs, so the relationship between each club and its meeting day is not represented as rows and columns.

**Task**

Replace the two meeting paragraphs with a table containing two data rows. Put Robotics and Tuesday in the first row, then Art and Thursday in the second row. Use `td` cells only in this step.
tryItExercises.hint: Create one table with two tr rows and two td cells in each row.

help.concept: Tables represent related values through rows and columns.
help.hint_2: Do not add caption or header cells yet.

tryItExercises.title: Add a caption and clear column headers
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The table has data rows, but visitors still need a clear table label and labels for the two columns.

**Task**

Keep both existing data rows. Add the caption **Weekly club meetings** and add a header row with `th` cells **Club** and **Day** above the data.
tryItExercises.hint: Add caption first, then a header tr with two th cells.

help.concept: A caption names the table and th cells identify column meaning.
help.hint_2: Add Club and Day as th cells in a new first row.

sketchBlocks.title: Separate headers from data with thead and tbody
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
`<thead>` groups header rows and `<tbody>` groups the main data rows. This makes a larger table easier to understand.

Use one `<tr>` per row and keep the same logical columns from row to row.

tryItExercises.title: Separate table headers from the data body
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The schedule already has its caption, header row, and all three data rows, but the header and data are not grouped into semantic table sections.

**Task**

Keep the caption and all cell content unchanged. Wrap the existing header row in `thead`, then wrap all three schedule rows in `tbody`.
tryItExercises.hint: Do not rebuild the table; only add thead around the header row and tbody around the data rows.

help.concept: thead groups header rows and tbody groups the table's data rows.
help.hint_1: Move only the header tr inside thead.
help.hint_2: Place all three data tr elements inside tbody.

quizDraft.title: Choose table markup for structured data
quizDraft.prompt: Which element represents one row in an HTML table?
quizDraft.hint: Think row, not cell or section.

help.concept: The tr element groups the cells that make up one table row.
help.hint_1: A td is one data cell.
help.hint_2: Choose the element whose name means table row.

quizDraft.title: Recognize table structure
quizDraft.hint: Choose elements whose purposes are part of table structure.

help.concept: th labels header cells and tbody groups body rows.
help.hint_1: One correct answer is a cell type; the other is a row group.
help.hint_2: Ignore elements from other HTML concepts.
